steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since your whitening with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still bright and white, a little staining coming back, or pretty much back to how it was. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Bright
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. Your notes say the color was really bothering you before we treated it. Is it nice to catch your smile in a photo and like it?

(Let them answer. This is their win.)

(Do not offer anything yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: A Little Staining Coming Back
steps.content:
That happens, {{contact_first_name}}, and you're right on track. Everyday life stains teeth for everyone. Coffee, tea, and wine all add a little over time. It's not the whitening failing. Your notes say you were really happy with the results. Does that sound right?

(Let them confirm. Stay warm. This is routine, not a problem.)

(Do not offer anything yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: Pretty Much Back to Before
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}, and please don't feel bad. Staining builds up. Every coffee and every glass of wine adds a little, and after enough time it settles back in. That's how teeth work for everyone, and it's easy to fix. Your notes say you were really happy with the results. What kept you from coming back in?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. It's nothing they did wrong.)

(Do not offer anything yet. Update the file first.)

steps.title: One More Thing: Sensitivity
steps.content:
Perfect, you're all set for (day) at (time).

(If you already asked about sensitivity during the file update, skip the question. Confirm the appointment and end the call.)

One quick thing while I have you, {{contact_first_name}}. Have you noticed any sensitivity to hot or cold, like with coffee or ice water?

(Let them answer.)

(If yes, read the next line.)

I'm glad you told me. That's common, and there's a lot we can do about it. I'll make a note so {{provider_name}} can plan your visit around it and keep it comfortable.

(If no, read the next line.)

Perfect, that makes everything easy. We'll see you (day) at (time), {{contact_first_name}}. Have a great day.

(Either way, end the call with the appointment confirmed.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm updating your file anyway. Can I ask you a few quick questions so it's up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to the staining in a moment. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment. Do not give dental advice on the call.)

First, the brightness. Is it still as bright as day one, or have you noticed a little dulling in photos?

How about coffee, tea, or red wine, still enjoying those about the same?

Any sensitivity to hot or cold?

Is there anything else about your smile you've wished were different?

Any big event coming up you'd want your smile ready for?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one would you most like to take care of?

(Tap their answer below. If nothing came up, that's still a good call. Use the second button.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment. Do not give dental advice on the call.)

First, the staining. When did you start noticing it?

How about coffee, tea, or red wine, still enjoying those about the same?

Any sensitivity to hot or cold?

Is there anything else about your smile you've wished were different?

Any big event coming up you'd want your smile ready for?

(Recap what you wrote down, including the staining, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between the staining and anything else you mentioned, which one would you most like to take care of?

(Tap their answer below. If getting the brightness back is the whole story, use the second button.)

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Recap what they told you: how long, how often, how it affects them.)

Did I get that right?

And it sounds like you'd like to feel good every time you catch your smile in a photo. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about what you just told me. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been on your mind, like a few weeks, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something that comes up now and then, or every time your smile is in a photo?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, smiling around people, or feeling confident?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Let them answer.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, it sounds like that's worth a look. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at that. If we can help, we'll tell you. If it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too. Does that sound reasonable?

(Say "does that sound reasonable", not "does that sound good". Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Stay Ahead of It
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad your smile is still looking bright.

One thing before I let you go. Staining comes back so slowly that you never see it happening. Coffee, tea, and wine dull things a shade at a time. Because you see your own smile every day, you're usually the last one to notice. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes. If they hesitate, use the second button.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you in for a quick touch-up. That way you stay ahead of the staining instead of chasing it. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let's find you a time. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Brightness Is the Whole Story: The Close
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, the nice thing is the whitening you did before is still working underneath. What's settled in since is newer surface stain, and newer stain lifts much easier than years of buildup. So getting the brightness back is a smaller job than the first time. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you in for that touch-up now. Getting back to that bright smile is one visit away. Does that sound reasonable?

(Wait for the yes.)

Okay, let's get you back on the books. I have (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: “I thought it would last longer”
steps.content:
That's a fair thing to bring up. Whitening looks great, but teeth pick up stain again over time from coffee, wine, and everyday foods. That's why coming in makes sense. {{provider_name}} can talk through how to get it bright again and help it last.

Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’m embarrassed it stained back up”
steps.content:
Please don't be. Staining builds up for everyone, one coffee at a time. That's the reason we call, and there's no judgment at all. We'd just like to help you get your smile back to where it was.

Would you be open to that?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: Sensitivity or a bad experience before
steps.content:
I'm glad you told me. That's the kind of thing {{provider_name}} will want to talk through in person. That way we can look at the whole picture and keep it comfortable.

(Do not give dental advice on the call.)

Is there anything else on your mind?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's right for them.

(Listen. Their answer usually points to one of the other objections. If it stays general, keep going.)

Coming in is really just information. You'd see what's possible and what it would involve, and then you decide with real answers. No pressure either way.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't show you what's possible for you specifically. That's what a quick visit is for. So let me get you on the schedule first, and then I'll send the information along.

Is that okay?
